subject: health
unitTitle: Relationships, Boundaries, and Support Networks Beyond High School
essentialQuestion: How do I build and keep a support network when the built-in one goes away?

prompts.prompt: Explain the shape of adult relationships: chosen, professional, and civic in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of holding boundaries with roommates, coworkers, and supervisors.
Apply consent and respect in adult contexts in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving recognizing coercive control and financial or social pressure; correct it and explain why.
Connect leaving an unsafe situation with a plan with building a support network deliberately rather than by accident. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design a named support network for a fictional graduate — who is contacted for what, what backup exists when a contact is unavailable, and what triggers escalation — then write two boundary scripts for adult settings.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: The network may be diagrammed, listed, dictated, or built on a supplied template. Scripts may be selected from a bank and adapted rather than composed.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
